newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended firmer with much of the market's attention focused on CS Group's new 10-year straight bond which was launched for 500 million Swiss francs, and increased later to 750 million.
The issue, which traders here believed was the largest ever corporate straight launched in Swiss francs, was seen as a success. "It was very well placed," said one trader.

"We wouldn't have reissued it if demand had not been good," a trader at CS said. It was also the first corporate issue for CS Group, formerly CS Holding, since the bank's major restructuring last year, Swiss traders said.
The bond's four percent coupon was also likely to be attractive to Swiss institutional investors.
The issue was quoted in late trade at minus 1.65 bid, yielding 4.0 percent.
Swiss government bond prices dipped, but only briefly after the CS issue was launched. The demand was seen buoyant enough to reduce selling pressure on Swiss Confederate bonds.
"The issue went so well that there was no real need to hedge" by selling government bonds, a trader said.
The June Conf bond futures contract ended firm but below the day's high of 119.10.

Shorter maturities were little changed. News the Swiss National Bank's M0 money supply grew above its target in the first quarter, by an annualised 9.2 percent versus the fourth quarter of 1996, had little impact on the market.
Comi medium-term bond COMIc1 down one at 111.04
Euro Swiss francs FESc1 up one at 98.10.
